primary_claim: No current unlearning technique (Gradient Difference, RMU, or Random Incorrect Answer) removes a significant fraction of targeted factual information from LLM weights: after fine-tuning on independent held-in facts, accuracy on held-out facts from the same set never comes close to halving, across four datasets (Years, MMLU cross-category split, WMDP-deduped, Random birthdays), even at unlearning coefficients strong enough to start destroying the model.

effect.metric: accuracy on held-out (V-split) facts after fine-tuning on independent (T-split) facts from the same dataset, across unlearning techniques
effect.value: no technique came close to halving held-out accuracy after retraining, across all 4 datasets tested, even at very large unlearning coefficients that begin destroying the model

contradicts_or_qualifies: Prior unlearning work evaluated success via probing failure or jailbreak robustness; the authors argue this is insufficient since new jailbreaks can extract information from models 'supposed to have had it removed' (e.g. WMDP-trained models), and show via an i.i.d. fine-tuning evaluation that current techniques do not actually remove information from weights

A separate paper claiming a fine-tuning-robust unlearning technique could not be reproduced by the authors, and appeared similar to another fine-tuning-robustness technique that can be broken with a better learning rate
stated_future_work: Teaching false facts by injecting fabricated information into training/pretraining data so the model cannot distinguish real from fake facts about a target topic (simplest version explored in the paper did not work)
Reversing memorization via mechanistic interpretability, given documents responsible for learning undesirable information (no concrete proposal yet)
Pre-training data filtering to prevent the information from entering the weights in the first place, though building a sufficiently precise filter is difficult
limitations_stated: The simplest version of the 'teaching false facts' approach explored in the paper did not work
A paper claiming a fine-tuning-robust unlearning technique could not be reproduced by the authors

Information removal cannot address application of allowed knowledge to disallowed use cases, nor prevent in-context learning/rediscovery of removed information, and this limitation will grow as AIs become more powerful
quote: No technique we tested can remove a significant fraction of the information from the weights.
